title: Regular sections and transverse direct sums
statement:
In the finite setting [def-pur-conventions], let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $F$ a locally free $\mathcal O_T$-module of constant rank $r\geq0$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Write $E(F)=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_T\operatorname{Sym}(F^\vee)$, with zero section $z$, in the convention [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. A section $s$ means an element of $\Gamma(T,F)$, equivalently the $T$-morphism $s:T\to E(F)$ induced by evaluation $\operatorname{Sym}(F^\vee)\to\mathcal O_T$. Its zero scheme is $Z(s)=T\times_{E(F),s,z}T$; its ideal is the image of $F^\vee\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal O_T$. The section is regular if for every $t\in Z(s)$ there is a local frame of $F$ at $t$ in which its $r$ components form an $\mathcal O_{T,t}$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Thus each component acts injectively modulo its predecessors, and the final quotient at $t$ is nonzero. No smoothness of $T$ or of $Z(s)$ over $k$ is part of this condition. The condition at an empty zero locus is vacuous. In rank zero the empty section has $Z(s)=T$.

For regular sections $s$ of $F$ and $t$ of $G$, a transverse direct sum means that in local frames at every point of $Z(s)\cap Z(t)$ the concatenated components of $(s,t)$ form a regular sequence. Its zero scheme is the scheme-theoretic intersection $Z(s)\times_TZ(t)$.
